answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may bid for work, then slash that stake when a bonded task is proven fraudulent through an auditable dispute process. Creating a hundred Sybils no longer multiplies influence for free: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it when caught. Honest agents can still cooperate, while a haven, oasis, or ridge in the network offers no exemption from the same bond rule.
